gen-flavors-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa spreads its sans letters wide, with curves that stay distinct. Flavors lands above it with whimsical diagonals as hefty as its stems, and that chunky, stubby-pencil weight is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-quantum-fs-merriweather-sans: Clean, techy lettering from Quantum sits loose and spacious, its mouths held wide open. And Merriweather Sans follows with tall, sturdy lowercase, so a long stretch of text would feel solid and large.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans stands tall and sturdy, its sans-serif e opening clearly. Starborn above it is dreamy, with wide gulfs between letters and a dark stripe of lowercase, and that gap in mood is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code runs on a wire-like monoline skeleton, with generous distance between neighbors and smooth paths around each bend. Autour One is the bold, expressive one, while the plain sans body just keeps going.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-cascadia-mono: Compact and pin-straight, Cascadia Mono has curves as thick as its stems and capitals that melt into lowercase. And Autour One brings bold, expressive round letters with a clear channel into each, so the page gets one loud voice and one tidy one.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-merriweather-sans: Gaping mouths on the e give Visitor its nostalgic, digital look, with strokes pulled like solder. But Merriweather Sans answers with sturdy, tall lowercase, and that chunky pixel-era versus roomy modern gap is the pair's best quality.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-hanuman: Tight, bold and modern, New Title locks its letters like links in a fine chain. But Hanuman brings the refined, traditional side, with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on the s, so one shouts while the other settles in.
gen-gf-goldman-fs-epilogue: Commanding Goldman spreads its round forms wide, like open parentheses, with a big lowercase beside its capitals. Epilogue then loosens things with curvy, marker-like strokes.
gen-gf-grandstander-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure, with an x-height that fills the line. Then General Sans meets Grandstander's bold, expressive letters, held open rather than curled shut, short on ascenders and tall in the lowercase.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-cascadia-mono: Expressive, spaghetti-like strokes give Funnel Display its voice. Shrink that heading and its same-width lines would still hold, while Cascadia Mono's pin-straight sans-serif letters would feel too wide if enlarged.
